faq.q: What is an intermediate and why adjustable?
faq.a: The intermediate is the block between the ram and a European-style punch that holds the clamp. The adjustable versions have a wedge that lets you set each section a few hundredths of a millimetre lower — manual crowning — so the angle stays the same along a long bend on a brake without automatic crowning. Z1 (27 mm body, axis 7 mm) and Z2 (40 mm body, axis 20 mm) differ in size: match the ones on your machine.

faq.q: Can one press brake use tooling of another style?
faq.a: Yes, through adapters: upper adapters take European-style punches on Trumpf / Wila, Beyeler, LVD, Weinbrenner, CBC, EHT, Durmazlar, Darley, Baykal and Colgar rams, and 4362 takes Trumpf / Wila punches on a European ram; lower adapters do the same for dies. An adapter adds height and costs some load capacity — check both before you buy.

faq.q: When is an adjustable die worth it?
faq.a: When you bend plate in many thicknesses: one 3191 covers V65 to V180 mm — the job of eight or ten solid dies — and the rollers on the shoulders reduce marking and force. For thin sheet and repeat work, solid 1V dies remain cheaper and more precise.
